newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends lower ahead of GCA stock data.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends lower ahead of GCA stock data.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended sharply lower on Friday, as locals and speculators sold in anticipation of a build up in U.S. warehouse inventories during July, traders said.

The Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock report, which will be released later today at 1500 EDT/1900 GMT, is expected to show an increase in U.S. green coffee stocks of 50,000 to 150,000 60-kg bags in July, traders said.
However, some dealers predicted a stock build of up to 250,000 bags.

"Basically, it was down on GCA. There is nervousness about how much supply there is," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "An increase breaks a historical trend. Stocks have seasonally gone down in July for the last three years."

September arabicas fell 6.60 cents per lb on the day, to a three-week low of 177.95 cents, after ranging from 186.00 to 175.25 cents. Active December ended 4.20 cents lower, to 161.85 cents, while the back months closed down 3.10 cents.

Coffee prices fell from the opening, as short-term speculators and some producers sold immediately, traders said. Downward momentum accelerated after September slipped through chart support near 178.00, triggering sell-stops.
Selling of the nearby September/December and December/March switches also pressured the market, they said.
September/December shrank to 16.10 cents compared with 18.50 cents at the close on Thursday. December/March 1998 narrowed to 15.75 cents versus 16.85 cents the previous session.

With September going into delivery period in less than a week, traders continued to see liquidation and rolling forward of September. As of Thursday, September open interest stood at 5,813 lots, down 383 lots from the previous session. December open interest increased by 315 lots, to 8,663 lots.
Technically, traders pegged September support at 175.00 cents, followed by 172.00 cents. Resistance was seen near 180.00 cents.

Traders await the bi-weekly CFTC Commitment of Traders report due after today's close. Refco's Prendergast said the data was likely to show a decline in speculative (non-commerical and nonreportable) long positions.
"I think the specs have gotton out of this market," she said. "I expect to see a 20 percent decrease in spec longs."
Volume on the day was fairly light, at an estimated 6,079 lots.
